subject: Information Theory
title: The Maximum Entropy Principle
description: A 60-second lesson on The Maximum Entropy Principle.

hook.text: You know a die's average is 3.5 but nothing else. What should you assume about each face? Maximum entropy decides.

buildup.text: The maximum entropy principle says: given constraints, choose the distribution that is most uncertain otherwise.

discovery.text: For a fair die with no extra info, uniform distribution wins. It assumes the least, commits the least.

twist.text: With constraints like a known mean, the max-entropy distribution isn't uniform—it's exponential or Gaussian.

climax.text: Jaynes showed this principle unifies statistical mechanics, Bayesian reasoning, and information theory.

punchline.text: When in doubt, assume maximum ignorance.

quiz.question: What does the maximum entropy principle recommend?
options: Choose the most uncertain distribution consistent with constraints
